ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, $AB=10$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. If $E$ is the midpoint of side $AD$ and $\angle AEO = 32^\circ$, what is the length of $OE$? What is the degree measure of $\angle ADO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: In diamond ABCD, AC and BD intersect at point O,\\
it follows that OA=OC, $\angle$ADB=$\angle$CDB, and CD=AB=10,\\
since E is the midpoint of side AD,\\
it follows AE=DE,\\
thus OE is the median line of $\triangle$ADC,\\
hence OE $\parallel$ CD, and OE=$\frac{1}{2}$CD=$\frac{1}{2} \times 10=\boxed{5}$,\\
therefore $\angle$ADC=$\angle$AEO=32$^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle$ADO=$\frac{1}{2}\angle$ADC=$\frac{1}{2} \times 32^\circ=\boxed{16^\circ}$,

method.method_draft: Use an analytic/vector model of the rhombus. From the diagram, take D as the origin, let vector DC be a horizontal side vector v and vector DA be another side vector u; then A=u, C=v, and B=u+v. From the text, |u|=|v|=AB=10 because ABCD is a rhombus, E is the midpoint of AD so E=u/2, and O is the intersection of diagonals, hence O=(A+C)/2=(u+v)/2. Then OE=|(u+v)/2-u/2|=|v|/2=5, and the direction of OE is the same as v, so OE is parallel to DC. Therefore angle AEO is the angle between EA, which is along u, and EO, which is along v, so it equals angle ADC=32 degrees. Since DO has direction u+v, and u and v have equal lengths, the vector u+v points along the internal angle bisector of the angle between u and v. Thus angle ADO is half of 32 degrees, giving 16 degrees.
